### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc32a4717e211b89bd1fe3fee750c4e43754089b` — the merge of head `4c02bddf8e26935368f9170ae5fb2487c9f2817b` into base `fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc32a4717e211b89bd1fe3fee750c4e43754089b && git checkout cc32a4717e211b89bd1fe3fee750c4e43754089b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a 4c02bddf8e26935368f9170ae5fb2487c9f2817b && git checkout -B drift-repro fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a && git merge --no-ff 4c02bddf8e26935368f9170ae5fb2487c9f2817b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa9c0aa2a0a8c2752f83b57765f3aae978ae196a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4c02bddf8e26935368f9170ae5fb2487c9f2817b`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 30429 --terms seedApplied,SeedLoadPartialWrites,landed` (report-only) to compare the body's line; no vitest, no build
Scope: the PR diff against merge-base `f506b79d85` (all 10 files, two commits `be4d35b5` and `4c02bddf`); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` at head (`SeedLoadPartialWrites` :578-600, `seedLoadPartialWrites` :609-611, `loadProgress` :764-767, `load` :809-819, `notePartialWrites` :827-841, `loadDatasets` :925-1090 with `allResults` :944-945 and the push :1062, `loadDataset` :1206-1223 and its return :2293-2327, the retry re-read :1375-1407, `resolveDeferredUpdates` :2603-2890); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-applied-landed.ts` (`SeedLandingResult` :24-28, `cappedList` :30-36, `seedAppliedLanded` :49-66); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts` (`applySeedBodies` :82-191, the lazy import :91-92, the returned path :139, the catch :141-190); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` :284-291; `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (:100, the fallback catch :2105-2153, `applyPublishedSeeds` :3847-3990); `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-seed-apply-landed-thrown.test.ts` (3 cases); `packages/objectql/src/publish-seed-receipt-landed-ids.test.ts` (harness :1-168, the two thrown pins :287-327, the old pin on main :287-300); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-seed-files.test.ts` :522-581; `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (`SEED_APPLIED_LANDED_DESCRIPTION` :1493-1501, the docblock :1534-1539, the two `landed` keys :1601 and :1902); `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts` :3034-3074; `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` :2549 and :2650; the generated-ledger census at `origin/main` (`packages/spec/json-schema.manifest/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, the three files that carry the `landed` description); `.changeset/30348-seed-receipt-landed-ids.md` and the new changeset; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` :1-80 and :900-945; the seat order `/mnt/project-files/seat3-orders/30429.md`; card #30429 body and 4 comments (triage 6657518253, the two claims, os-dev-report 6659938998); PR #30427's contract review 6656296448; PR #30519 body, 2 comments, 0 reviews; check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The partial-writes path carries the finished datasets' ids, and both producers fold them through the one projection. `loadProgress.finished` IS `allResults` (:945), a dataset's result is pushed only after `loadDataset` returns (:1062, return at :2311), and the dataset loading when the throw hits sits in `loading` (:1223) and never in `finished`; so `notePartialWrites` (:836) snapshots exactly the datasets that finished, in load order, taking `object`, `landedIds` and `insertedIds` off each result. The id arrays are built once at :2293-2308 and nothing writes to them afterwards (pass 2 touches `referencesResolved` and the error lists on `allResults`, the #30427 review's reading, re-confirmed by the `allResults` census at :2662 and :2890), so copying the references is safe and the "snapshot of the ids alone" comment (:834-835) is right about what it protects against. `applySeedBodies`' catch adds `...(written ? { landed: seedAppliedLanded(written.finished) } : {})` (:177), the same function the returned path calls at :139, and `seedAppliedLanded` is the only place `cappedList` (:30-36) and the inserted-versus-matched split (:61-65) live; `SeedLandingResult` is imported as a type from the projection module (:51), so no second copy of the shape either. One projection, same two lists, same 200 cap. The loader's `catch` wraps every throw out of `load` (:816-818), including one before `loadProgress` is set (:936-942), so every error that came out of a load carries a reading.
2. The failing dataset is omitted, and the reason holds. The loader's batched flush re-reads existing rows by key on `attempt > 1` because a prior attempt may have committed before its response was lost (:1402-1406); a throw that lands inside or right after such a flush leaves `internalIdByRecordIndex` short of rows the table holds, so a list of the ids the loader did see for that dataset would read as complete while missing rows. A finished dataset has no such hole. The seed-files pin measures the concrete case: `pw_doc`'s D1 is in the store when the storage service throws (:559-560) and `finished` names `pw_tag` only (:566-568). The reason is stated in the `finished` docblock (:592-597), the catch comment (:173-176), the spec docblock (:1536-1538) and the body; the describe (:1498-1499) states the rule (not listed; rows in the counts, object in `error`) without the reason, which is the right split for a wire description. Empty versus absent: `finished` is `[]` whenever no dataset finished (:828, :836), so any throw out of `load` reports `landed: []`, and `landed` is absent only when the error did not come out of a load: the request parse refusal (:127), the loader import (:91), and in the runtime `required services unavailable` (:3859), a seed-body read failure (:3886) and `no readable seed bodies` (:3950). The describe's "the apply failed before any load ran" is exactly that set. `[]` is consistent with the returned-load path: a request whose datasets all filter out returns `buildEmptyResult` (:981) with no results, so the returned receipt also says `landed: []` for "the loader ran, no object ran"; "one entry per object the loader ran, empty lists included" covers both. The describe does not spell the `[]` case out; the changeset and the objectql pin at :315-327 do (should-fix 2).
3. The runtime fallback gets the same fix the same way. `applyPublishedSeeds` has the same thrown path (`loader.load` :3981 with no catch of its own, caught at the door :2105); the door's catch now reads `seedLoadPartialWrites(e)` (:2134) and spreads `landed: seedAppliedLanded(written.finished)` (:2138) through the same two symbols imported from the package root (:100; `index.ts` :284-291 exports the reader and its type). What the fallback still does not carry is `inserted` / `updated` on a throw (:2135-2152), although `PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema.seedApplied` declares both required and the new describe says the failing dataset's "rows are in the counts". The body names this as pre-existing and carried; it is, but `written` is now in hand at :2134 and the counts are two more spreads (should-fix 1).
4. Spec and ripples. The shared describe (:1493-1501) and the `PublishMetaItemResponseSchema` docblock (:1534-1539) say what a thrown load reports (finished datasets only; the one that threw not listed, rows in the counts, object in `error`) and when `landed` is still absent (no load ran, or a producer that reports no ids); the schema shape is byte-identical (:1601, :1902 unchanged). Ripples: on `origin/main` exactly three files carry the description text (the #30348 changeset, `protocol.zod.ts`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`); the mdx's two cells (:2549, :2650) now carry the new describe verbatim, which is the generator's output, not a hand edit. `json-schema.manifest/api.json` is a name list (no description hashes), `api-surface/api.json` lists spec symbols (none added), and the llms route builds from the mdx at docs build time, so no other committed artifact owes a change. `check:generated` exit 0 in the dev's report; `Lint · docs & code guards` was `in_progress` at review time.
5. Pins and ablations. objectql, real protocol over a real engine and the real loader: the old pin (main :287-300, `'landed' in res.seedApplied` false) is replaced by :287-313, where a customer row shares `R1`'s key so both lists are exercised, `a_good` lands three records (`inserted: 2`, created ids read back from the engine, `matched: [customer.id]`), `z_missing` throws, `error` names it, `landed` has one entry and no entry for the object that threw, and `PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema.parse` keeps it on a failed apply (:311); :315-327 pins `landed: []` when the first dataset throws. Runtime, the real `HttpDispatcher` and the real `SeedLoaderService` over a mocked engine: positive control, a second dataset's existing-row read throwing after the first wrote (`find` asserted called on `BROKEN`), and `getMetaItem` failing before any load with `'landed' in seedApplied` false (:87-116). Loader unit: `finished` with the store's own ids and the written-but-unfinished `pw_doc` left out (:561-568), `finished: []` before any dataset (:580). Ablation A (the snapshot neutralised in dist) reddens 1/10, 1/3, 1/3 and ablation B (the catch spread neutralised) reddens 2/10, each with blob hashes and a restore leg; the counts match the reading (A cannot redden the `[]` pin, B reddens both thrown pins). Both real. The spec pin at `protocol.test.ts` :3050-3056 asserts absence on a hand-built receipt that carries no `landed`, not on a thrown load, so it is correct as left. Gap: no pin for a throw in pass 2 (`resolveDeferredUpdates` :1082), where every dataset finished, `failedObject` is unset and `landed` lists them all; by reading that is what :828-836 and :167-169 give (should-fix 3).
6. Declarations. Body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; the changeset grades spec `minor`, metadata-protocol `minor`, runtime `patch`. Under the gate's rule (:909-910) a kind needs at least one moved package at `minor` or above, which two entries meet; `Check Changeset` is green on the head, and the dev's controls (`none` exits 1, `added` exits 0) show the gate checks the level, not the kind. `semantic` over `added` is right by reading: no authorable key, value or default is added (no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves, the schema shape is unchanged), and what moves is the meaning of an existing key's absence on a thrown load (from "not reported, including a load that threw" to "no load ran"), which is the kind the gate's own text calls "a changed meaning" (:931). metadata-protocol `minor` is earned by its own surface: two new root exports (`seedLoadPartialWrites`, `SeedLoadPartialWrites`) and a new required member `finished` on an exported record. The "Supersedes" paragraph names the sentence in the unreleased #30348 changeset this makes false, so the release notes will not carry two contradictory readings of absent `landed`.
7. Scope, body and lines. No cloud file; `claim-seed-ownership.ts` and `seed-settlement.ts` are not in the diff and still read `landedIds`. The body's four-row table of what `landed` answers matches :139, :177 and the loader's `finished` by reading; the "no reading" cases it names (parse refusal, loader import) are :127 and :91. `Prior rulings read:` is byte-identical to the script's output on the same terms. The 维护者速读 has its six lines and its two-minute check names the objectql file at 10/10, the count the ablation report also gives. 234 changed lines, no governed surface in the file list.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/runtime` patch, with `Metadata-protocol: semantic` and `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The receipt widens (a failed apply now carries an optional key it did not), no shape changes, and an existing key's absence narrows in meaning; the level follows the kind, and the changeset's grades are the ones the gate owes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The line the change draws (finished datasets listed, the failing one not) is the card's default and the safe direction for cloud's "clear sample data": every id listed is one the loader is certain of, and a reader can tell unlisted rows exist by comparing `inserted` with the listed `inserted.total`s, as the body says. That comparison needs the counts, which the runtime fallback's thrown receipt does not carry (judgment 3).
- `finished` is a required member of `SeedLoadPartialWrites`; the only constructor is `notePartialWrites`, so no other producer has to be taught it. A consumer that narrows the record (the ownership claim) is out of scope and untouched.
- The runtime pin drives a mocked engine; the real-engine pin for the same receipt key is the objectql one, and the two producers share the reader and the projection by import, so the fallback's door pin is a producer pin, not an engine pin. Acceptable.
- Carried tier: the fallback's missing counts on a throw (pre-existing, named in the body's Acceptance notes, no card filed); the failing dataset's own landed rows have no ids on the receipt (cloud's reading, out of scope here).

### ④ Design judgment

The fix is at the right layer (the loader's own partial-writes record, which already held the finished results) and keeps the shape #30348 set: one projection, two lists, one cap, two producers importing the same two symbols. The failing-dataset decision is argued from the loader's own retry rule rather than asserted, and every claim the order makes is pinned at a real door with real reds. Must-fix: none. Should-fix, in order: (1) in the runtime fallback's catch, spread `inserted: written?.inserted ?? 0` and `updated: written?.updated ?? 0` beside `landed` now that `written` is read there (:2134), so the schema's required counts are met and the describe's "its rows are in the counts" is true of both producers; failing that, file the carried card and name it in the body; (2) add "possibly empty, when the throw came before any dataset finished" to the describe (:1498-1499), since the changeset and the objectql pin promise `[]` and the describe only implies it; (3) add a loader-unit or door pin for a throw in pass 2 (every dataset finished, no `failedObject`, `landed` lists all); (4) harmonize the older catch comment at `protocol-publish-batch.ts` :155-160 ("No reading means the throw came before the loader wrote anything") with the new one at :170-176 ("no load ran"), since the first now reads as the only condition and is the weaker of the two. None blocks landing; landing waits on the still-running required contexts (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1-8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint`) going green.
